subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: During the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, the radical preacher who demanded greater equality was who?
questions.explain: John Ball preached against feudal inequality, famously asking who was the gentleman in Eden.

questions.q: What was the main cause of the 1926 General Strike?
options: A dispute over miners' wages and working hours
questions.explain: The General Strike began in support of coal miners facing wage cuts and longer hours.

questions.q: The Great Reform Act of 1832 did what?
options: Redistributed seats and modestly widened the franchise
questions.explain: The 1832 Reform Act removed some 'rotten boroughs' and extended the vote to more middle-class men.

questions.q: Women in Britain gained the vote on the same terms as men in which year?
questions.explain: The 1928 Act extended the vote to all women over 21, on equal terms with men.

questions.q: The 1819 Peterloo Massacre occurred when cavalry charged a crowd demanding what?
questions.explain: At Peterloo in 1819, troops charged a peaceful meeting calling for political reform, killing several.

questions.q: The Second Reform Act of 1867 mainly extended the vote to which group?
questions.explain: The 1867 Reform Act gave the vote to many working men in towns, roughly doubling the electorate.

questions.q: Magna Carta of 1215 included the principle that the king could not do what without lawful judgement?
questions.explain: Magna Carta stated no free man could be imprisoned except by lawful judgement, an early protection of rights.

questions.q: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was triggered largely by which grievance?
questions.explain: Resentment at the Poll Tax sparked the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, led by Wat Tyler.

questions.q: The Suffragettes, led by Emmeline Pankhurst, were known for what type of campaign?
options: Militant, direct action such as protests and hunger strikes
questions.explain: The Suffragettes (WSPU) used militant tactics, unlike the law-abiding Suffragists.

questions.q: The 1834 Tolpuddle Martyrs were eventually pardoned after what happened?
options: A large public campaign and petitions in their support
questions.explain: A huge public campaign and petitions led to the Tolpuddle Martyrs being pardoned and returned home.

questions.q: The 'Glorious Revolution' of 1688 led to which key constitutional document the following year?
questions.explain: The 1689 Bill of Rights limited royal power and strengthened Parliament after 1688.

questions.q: King Charles I was tried and executed in which year following the English Civil War?
questions.explain: Charles I was executed in 1649, the only English king to be put on trial and beheaded.

questions.q: The Chartists of the 1830s-40s campaigned mainly for what?
options: Political reforms including votes for all men
questions.explain: The People's Charter demanded reforms such as universal manhood suffrage and a secret ballot.

questions.q: In 1918, the Representation of the People Act gave the vote to which women?
options: Women over 30 who met a property qualification
Only women who had served in the war
questions.explain: The 1918 Act gave the vote to women over 30 with a property qualification; equality came in 1928.

questions.q: During the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, who was the rebels' main leader killed at Smithfield?
questions.explain: Wat Tyler led the rebels and was killed during the confrontation with Richard II at Smithfield.

questions.q: The General Strike took place in Britain in which year?
questions.explain: The General Strike of 1926 saw millions stop work in support of the coal miners.

questions.q: Simon de Montfort is remembered in 1265 for summoning what, a step towards representative government?
options: The first Parliament including elected commoners
questions.explain: In 1265 Simon de Montfort summoned a parliament that included knights and townsmen, an early step toward representation.

questions.q: The secret ballot, ending open voting at elections, was introduced in Britain by which 1872 measure?
questions.explain: The Ballot Act of 1872 introduced secret voting, reducing bribery and intimidation at elections.

questions.q: The Tolpuddle Martyrs of 1834 were punished for doing what?
questions.explain: Six Dorset labourers were transported for swearing a secret oath to form a trade union.

questions.q: The Bill of Rights of 1689 established which important principle?
options: That bishops should sit in the Commons
That trial by ordeal would return
That the monarch could not rule or raise taxes without Parliament
questions.explain: The Bill of Rights made the monarch subject to Parliament's consent for laws, taxes and armies.

questions.q: The peaceful campaigners for women's suffrage, led by Millicent Fawcett, were known as the what?
questions.explain: The Suffragists (NUWSS) used lawful, peaceful methods, unlike the militant Suffragettes.

questions.q: Magna Carta, which limited the power of the king, was sealed by King John in which year?
questions.explain: King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215 after pressure from rebellious barons.
